entries.text: This project ships instructions and data plus an executable runtime: the catalog and skills are instructions, .opencode/plugin/arsenal.ts is a real TypeScript runtime with seven registered hook callbacks that write to disk and spawn processes, and scripts is a set of executable programs.

The install_cmd fields are the highest-value target because an automated agent typically runs them; the two failure modes are a command that looks right but is wrong, and a command that was correct when written and has since changed upstream through squatted names, renamed repos, or handed-over ownership.

An install command is never invented: it is verified against a real registry and marked verification verified, or it is marked verification unverified which may still carry a mechanically derived command, or it is null; agents, plugins, and hooks carry null plus verification unverified; a verified flag records that a command was checked and stays an assertion to re-test rather than auditable proof; the lock pins versions only where a version_pin exists; and scripts/verify-kit.mjs re-proves that each component resolves.

Secrets live in environment variables or a secret manager and never in this repository; the tooling reads VANTRILEX_STATE_DIR, the pre-commit hook refuses a newly added .env file while the credential-shape scan still runs on added lines of every file, and a committed credential is revoked or rotated first and only then removed.

You report a vulnerability privately through the repository Security advisory form and never open a public issue for an unfixed vulnerability; you include the component id, the affected version, what an attacker gains, and a reproduction when you have one, and you receive an acknowledgement within 72 hours.

You scope destructive operations to your own worktree or an explicitly named path inside the project, and force pushes, history rewrites, recursive deletions, and schema or data drops require explicit approval recorded before execution; every deletion in scripts resolves inside the repository root and worktree slugs stay inside [a-z0-9]; versions 0.2.x and 0.1.x are supported, below 0.1.0 is not, and the pre-1.0 Registry format may still change in a breaking way.
